extracted.intended_audience: newsroom leaders, editors, journalists, and journalism professional organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how news organizations should handle incidents of plagiarism, fabrication, and major errors — covering transparency, investigation, policy creation, education, and spot-checking practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in handling ethical breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders in a profession dedicated to shining a light on truth need to meet the same standard of transparency they demand of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about incidents to strengthen trust with sources and the public; avoid vague public statements and stonewalling which embolden others to hide wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name the people involved and acknowledge discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: When ethical breaches occur, news organizations should not withhold the names of those involved or refuse to acknowledge related discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics about who committed offenses and what disciplinary actions were taken unless there is a compelling legal/HR reason; avoiding naming and discipline details is corrosive to accountability (examples: New Canaan News, Boston Globe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer questions from the press; avoid 'no comment' reflex
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should respond to inquiries rather than reflexively issuing 'no comment' or offering only extremely brief statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to legitimate questions to prevent perception of cover-up; the author notes personal frustration when outlets refuse to answer basic queries about incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create clear guidelines and processes for handling plagiarism, fabrication, and major errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should have basic, explicit policies and processes that specify how to investigate and respond to plagiarism, fabrication, and major mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an omnibus set of best practices that cover detection, investigation, discipline, disclosure, internal/external communication, and follow-up; the lack of clear guidance contributes to inconsistent and harmful responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional organizations should collaborate on unified best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading journalism organizations' ethics committees/boards should gather existing policies and create cross-organizational guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups like SPJ, ACES, ASNE, APME should collaborate to produce a unified set of best practices applicable across mediums and newsroom sizes; solicit existing newsroom policies to inform the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and promote the resulting best practices widely
rubrics_metrics.description: Once best practices exist, they must be published and actively promoted so newsrooms adopt them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsroom leaders should vocally support and endorse the guidance to signal a new standard from the top and help create a culture of transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute random plagiarism checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should run a selection of published content per week through a plagiarism detection service of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate to staff that checks are being performed to ensure adherence to policy and to deter transgressions; the checks are described as straightforward and affordable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute random fabrication/source-verification checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should randomly select published pieces and contact sources to verify quotes and factual claims; ideally, do this prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acts as a deterrent and helps catch fabrication; verification prior to publication is preferable to catch errors earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate past work of implicated journalists as part of review
rubrics_metrics.description: When plagiarism or fabrication is found, organizations should review the subject’s past work for other problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Time/CNN reviewed Fareed Zakaria's past work; Wired examined Jonah Lehrer's previously published material — these reviews inform whether broader action is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full public accounting of incidents when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should publish a complete accounting of significant transgressions rather than minimal, reluctant brief notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full accounts help the public understand the scope and nature of problems (example: New Canaan News published only a 152-word brief which was criticized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use communications/public relations without letting PR substitute for accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s appropriate to have communications colleagues draft and distribute statements, but PR should not be used to hide or minimize incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications staff can provide useful guidance, but leadership must not hide behind message control; statements should be factual and transparent, not evasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a consistent process for investigating and communicating internally and externally
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a standardized investigation procedure and communication protocol for incidents that applies across the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consistent process reduces ad hoc responses and ensures fairness, clarity for staff, and clear messages to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate newsrooms about ethics policies and new best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Once guidelines exist, the profession should work to educate newsrooms and spread awareness of the practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training and materials; leaders should promote adoption so the policies change newsroom culture and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat plagiarism and fabrication as preventable through deterrence and checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular audits and verification are framed as deterrents and practical ways to reduce incidents of cheating and fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make staff aware of random checks and verification processes to discourage misconduct and catch those already engaging in unethical behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise language (call things 'plagiarism' or 'fabrication' when they are such)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets should not avoid labeling incidents accurately (for example, avoiding the word 'plagiarism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate labels help the public and profession understand the severity and nature of the transgression; euphemistic language undermines accountability (example: Boston Globe’s reluctance to use the word plagiarism).
